resources.string: Set up and control a Debian 13 server that starts before Android’s first unlock and stays running afterward. Complete the sections from top to bottom once; routine controls and SSH access remain easy to reach.
Grant permanent Magisk access, enable automatic startup, then save the BFU runtime.
Install Debian 13 and configure systemd, OpenSSH, and the generated access key.
Check the current state or explicitly start, restart, and stop the Debian environment.
Export the generated key or copy ready-to-run commands for a local Termux client.
Optionally set local Debian passwords. SSH continues to accept public keys only.
BFU probes, operation history, and the unsafe CE override are hidden during normal use.
Destructive actions require a second confirmation and are never run automatically.
Unsafe: allow BFU when this app’s CE storage is readable

Leave this disabled on correctly configured FBE devices. Enable it only when the BFU sentinel proves this ROM exposes CE before first unlock and you accept that platform-level risk. It never bypasses encryption; it only permits Debian startup after recording a warning.

App-generated BFU SSH client public key. A random Ed25519 key is created automatically after unlock. Only this public line is provisioned into Device Protected Storage and Debian authorized_keys; the private half remains in this app’s Credential Protected Storage until you explicitly export it.
Could not load or generate the SSH client key: %1$s
Unlock Android before accessing or changing the SSH client key.
Generate a new random SSH client key
Replace the BFU SSH client key?

The current private key will be permanently replaced. Its public key is updated in app DE storage immediately, but you must run Configure Debian 13 systemd + SSH again before the new key can log in. Existing exported copies will stop working after reconfiguration.
The new public key is saved in BFU storage. Run Configure Debian 13 systemd + SSH to install it into Debian, then export/import the new private key into your SSH client.

Debian boot requires Magisk root on every cold boot. Authorize the standalone DawnShell app while Android is unlocked, and choose Magisk’s permanent/forever option so no approval UI is needed during BFU.
Last AFU root authorization check (not BFU proof):\n%1$s
No interactive root authorization check has been recorded.
Failed to read root authorization result: %1$s
Unlock Android first so Magisk can show its authorization UI.

Magisk stores root policy by Linux UID. Granting UID %1$s therefore grants root to all installed packages sharing it:

%2$s

Continue only if every listed app is trusted. In Magisk, select the permanent/forever duration; a one-time grant will not work after a cold reboot.
Waiting for Magisk authorization. Approve the request with the permanent/forever duration…

UID %1$s successfully executed as uid=0. This proves root works now, but the app cannot determine whether Magisk saved a permanent policy. Confirm “Allow” with permanent/forever duration in Magisk before the BFU reboot test.
Magisk did not return uid=0. Check that Magisk root access is enabled for apps, then retry.\n\nResult: %1$s
No root probe has been recorded yet.
Failed to read BFU root result: %1$s
No CE isolation probe has been recorded yet. Save and provision while unlocked to create the non-secret CE sentinel; BFU launch fails closed if its contents can be read.
Failed to read BFU CE isolation result: %1$s
No rootfs probe has been recorded yet.
Failed to read BFU rootfs result: %1$s
No namespace/chroot probe has been recorded yet. It runs automatically during the next locked boot after the rootfs gate passes.
Failed to read BFU namespace/chroot result: %1$s
BFU button and operation log (live, newest 48 KiB):
No button operation has been recorded yet.
Failed to read or write the operation log: %1$s
Drag inside a console to scroll it. Long-press to select and copy. Live follow pauses while selected or scrolled up.

Rootfs installation runs only after unlock. In Termux, first run: pkg install debootstrap util-linux mount-utils. The app downloads pinned official Debian artifacts, verifies SHA-256, and builds a staging tree before publishing /data/local/debian.
Unlock Android before deleting the Debian rootfs.

This first stops the standalone Debian supervisor, verifies that no systemd process remains, then permanently deletes exactly /data/local/debian. All Debian packages, users, password hashes, SSH host keys, and in-rootfs configuration will be lost. App DE settings and logs are retained.
Type DELETE exactly to authorize permanent rootfs removal.
Confirmation did not match DELETE. Nothing was removed.
Rootfs removal requested. Follow the live operation log.
Enable Direct Boot Debian bootstrap before installing.
Unlock Android before installing the Debian rootfs.

This downloads Debian 13 Trixie packages and runs upstream debootstrap as pre-authorized Magisk root. Existing /data/local/debian is never overwritten or upgraded in place. Keep this app open to watch the live log.
Debian installation requested. Live output appears below.
No Debian installation has been requested yet.

After the Trixie rootfs install succeeds, this AFU-only step installs systemd, D-Bus, and OpenSSH. It creates user debian, copies the validated DE public keys, disables password/root login, enables ssh.service on TCP 22, masks Android-host-sensitive units, and writes the BFU-ready marker only after validation.
Unlock Android before configuring Debian packages.

This temporarily stops a running BFU Debian instance, uses apt inside /data/local/debian, and then starts the configured system again for validation. SSH accepts only the public keys shown above. Keep this app open to watch the live log.
Debian system configuration requested. Live output appears below.
Could not request Debian system configuration: %1$s
No Debian system configuration has been requested yet.
Failed to read system configuration status: %1$s
Debian system configuration log (live, newest 48 KiB):

Debian starts automatically during LOCKED_BOOT_COMPLETED after all BFU gates pass. USER_UNLOCKED never stops or restarts it. Start, restart, and status also verify systemd PID 1, D-Bus, ssh.service, and TCP 22; results are persisted in the DE log.
This explicitly asks the Debian container service manager to exit gracefully and stops SSH. Unlock events do not perform this action.
This gracefully exits the verified Debian PID 1, starts a fresh isolated instance, then waits for D-Bus, SSH, and TCP 22 health checks. USER_UNLOCKED never performs this action.
Could not request Debian lifecycle operation: %1$s
No Debian lifecycle operation has been recorded yet.
Failed to read Debian lifecycle status: %1$s
Debian systemd lifecycle log (live, newest 64 KiB):

Local Debian account passwords (AFU only). Values are sent directly to Debian chpasswd and are never saved in Android preferences, BFU storage, or logs. SSH remains public-key-only. Setting the root password allows “su root” inside Debian and grants device-level root authority; use a unique strong password.
Unlock Android before changing a Debian password.
Another password update is still running.
The password and confirmation do not match. Both fields were cleared.
Local Debian %1$s password updated. The password was not stored by the app.
Could not update local Debian %1$s password: %2$s
Anyone who obtains this unencrypted file can log in as debian while the key is authorized. Store it only in a trusted location and restrict its permissions to 0600.
SSH private key exported. Restrict it to owner-only access before use.
Could not export the SSH private key: %1$s
Place the private key on the clipboard?

The copied one-line command contains the complete private key. Paste it only into your own unlocked Termux session. The app marks it sensitive and clears it after 120 seconds if it is still the current clipboard entry.
Private-key import command copied. Paste it into Termux now; the clipboard entry expires in 120 seconds.
SSH connect command copied. Paste and run it in Termux.
Keeps the Direct Boot bootstrap lifecycle active for the Android boot.
Direct Boot Debian supervisor active; USER_UNLOCKED does not stop it
Settings changed — apply them before rebooting.
